title: Topic 1.4: Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORIES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can you predict the outcome of a story even before you read it?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words
2. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words
   In simple words: practise until you can use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story
   In simple words: practise until you can answer direct and inferential questions from a short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
4. Show that you can: use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Predict events by focusing on the title and illustrations in a text,
2. Silently read the short story,
3. Role-play selected events and characters in the story,
4. Critical thinking: It is promoted as the learner assesses the relationship between their own lives and those of the characters in the story.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you predict the outcome of a story even before you read it?
2. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words in a story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words
2. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
